requirements.original: If in an unmap operation a param clause is present, exactly one of the components referenced by the operation shall be the system component reference, the type of the system component shall be known in the context of the operation either via a system clause or via a runs on clause in a testcase without system clause, the type of the system port to which the operation is applied shall include an unmap param declaration and the actual parameters shall conform to the unmap **param clause of the port type declaration of the system port used.** c) If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (either when the component reference is a variable or value returned from a function or the type is defined the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration shall be present in this component type.

requirements.subject: ent:port-declaration
requirements.condition: the component type of the referenced component is known
requirements.canonical: If the type of a component referenced in a `disconnect` or `unmap` operation is known (the component reference is a variable or a value returned from a function, or the type is defined in the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port SHALL be declared in that component type.
requirements.original: If in an unmap operation a param clause is present, exactly one of the components referenced by the operation shall be the system component reference, the type of the system component shall be known in the context of the operation either via a system clause or via a runs on clause in a testcase without system clause, the type of the system port to which the operation is applied shall include an unmap param declaration and the actual parameters shall conform to the unmap **param clause of the port type declaration of the system port used.** c) If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (either when the component reference is a variable or value returned from a function or the type is defined the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration shall be present in this component type.

ambiguity.issue: 'connection operation' is not a defined term; in clause 21.1.2 it refers to disconnect and unmap.

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: The parameters of a `disconnect` operation SHALL NOT contain a system port reference.
requirements.original: d) The disconnect operation parameters shall not contain a system port reference.

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-operation
requirements.canonical: A test case operation addresses the entire test case by using the keyword `testcase`.
requirements.original: Test case operations address the entire test case by using the keyword testcase.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation IS the only test case operation.
requirements.original: Currently, the test case stop operation is the only test case operation.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation specifies an immediate stop of the test case behaviour with the verdict `error`.
requirements.original: It specifies an immediate stop of the test case behaviour with an error verdict.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation causes a user-defined immediate termination of a test case with the test verdict `error`.
requirements.original: The testcase stop operation defines a user defined immediate termination of a test case with the test verdict error and an (optional) associated reason for the termination.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation MAY specify an optional reason for the termination.
requirements.original: The testcase stop operation defines a user defined immediate termination of a test case with the test verdict error and an (optional) associated reason for the termination.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation IS intended for cases where user-defined behaviour that does not contribute to the test outcome behaves unexpectedly so that continuing the test case makes no sense.
requirements.original: Such an immediate stop of a test case is required for cases where a user defined behaviour that does not contribute to the test outcome behaves in an unexpected manner which leads to a situation where the continuation of the test case makes no more sense.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation has the syntax testcase . stop optionally followed by a parenthesized comma-separated list of FreeText or TemplateInstance items.
requirements.original: testcase "." stop [ "(" { ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) [","] } ")" ]

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation causes an immediate stop of the entire test case behaviour with the verdict `error`.
requirements.original: The test case stop operation causes an immediate stop of the entire test case behaviour with the verdict error.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation writes the items in its argument, specifying the reason for the termination, to a logging device associated with the test control or the test component in which the operation is used.
requirements.original: In addition, the test case stop operation provides the means to specify the reason for the immediate termination of a test case by writing one or more items to some logging device associated with the test control or the test component in which the operation is used.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The items to be logged by a test case stop operation SHALL be given as a comma-separated list in the argument of the operation.
requirements.original: Items to be logged shall be identified by a comma-separated list in the argument of the test case stop operation.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The argument of the test case stop operation SHALL follow the same restrictions as the argument of the `log` statement.
requirements.original: The argument of the test case stop operation shall follow the same restrictions as the argument of the log statement (see clause 19.11).

requirements.subject: ent:test-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Test component operations are used to create, start, stop and kill test components.
requirements.original: Test component operations are used to create, start, stop and kill test components.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Test component operations are also used to check whether test components are alive, running, done or killed.
requirements.original: They can also be used to check if test components are alive, running, done or killed.

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The `create` operation IS the operation used to create test components.
requirements.original: The create operation is used to create test components.

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The `create` operation has the syntax ComponentType "." `create` [ "(" Expression ["," Expression] ")" ] [ `alive` ].
requirements.original: ComponentType "." create [ "(" Expression ["," Expression] ")" ] [ alive ]

requirements.subject: ent:mtc
requirements.canonical: The MTC IS the only test component that is created automatically when a test case starts.
requirements.original: The MTC is the only test component, which is automatically created when a test case starts.

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: A PTC SHALL be created explicitly during test execution by a `create` operation.
requirements.original: All other test components (the PTCs) shall be created explicitly during test execution by create operations.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A newly created test component IS created with its full set of ports, the input queues of which are empty.
requirements.original: A component is created with its full set of ports of which the input queues are empty and with its full set of constants, variables and timers.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A newly created test component IS created with its full set of component constants, component variables and component timers.
requirements.original: A component is created with its full set of ports of which the input queues are empty and with its full set of constants, variables and timers.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.condition: the port is defined to be of the type in or inout
requirements.canonical: A port whose port type allows incoming (in or inout) communication SHALL be in a listening state, ready to receive traffic over the connection, when the component is created.
requirements.original: Furthermore, if a port is defined to be of the type in or inout it shall be in a listening state ready to receive traffic over the connection.

ambiguity.issue: Ports are not 'of the type in or inout'; the intended meaning is a port whose port type declares in or inout messages/signatures.

improper_terms.used: port ... of the type in or inout
improper_terms.proper: port whose port type declares in or inout messages or signatures

requirements.subject: ent:component-variable
requirements.canonical: When a test component is explicitly or implicitly created, every component variable and component timer IS reset to its initial value, if any.
requirements.original: All component variables and timers are reset to their initial value (if any) and all component constants are reset to their assigned values when the component is explicitly or implicitly created.

requirements.subject: ent:component-constant
requirements.canonical: When a test component is explicitly or implicitly created, every component constant IS reset to its assigned value.
requirements.original: All component variables and timers are reset to their initial value (if any) and all component constants are reset to their assigned values when the component is explicitly or implicitly created.

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: A PTC IS either a non-alive PTC, which can execute a behaviour only once, or an alive-type PTC, which is kept alive after termination of a behaviour and can therefore be reused to execute another behaviour.
requirements.original: Two types of PTCs are distinguished: a PTC that can execute a behaviour only once and a PTC that is kept alive after termination of a behaviour and can be therefore reused to execute another behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: An alive-type PTC IS created using the `create` operation with the additional `alive` keyword.
requirements.original: The latter is created using the additional alive keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: An alive-type PTC SHALL be destroyed explicitly using the `kill` operation.
requirements.original: An alive-type PTC shall be destroyed explicitly using the kill operation (see clause 21.3.4), whereas a non-alive PTC is destroyed implicitly after its behaviour terminates.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether this obliges the test writer to kill alive-type PTCs or only states that an alive-type PTC is not destroyed implicitly when its behaviour terminates (test case termination destroys it anyway, see 21.3.1-s011). The second reading is chosen.
readings: An alive-type PTC IS NOT destroyed implicitly when its behaviour terminates; it is destroyed only by the `kill` operation or by the termination of the test case.
The test writer SHALL kill every alive-type PTC explicitly using the `kill` operation before the test case ends.

requirements.subject: ent:non-alive-ptc
requirements.canonical: A non-alive PTC IS destroyed implicitly after its behaviour terminates.
requirements.original: An alive-type PTC shall be destroyed explicitly using the kill operation (see clause 21.3.4), whereas a non-alive PTC is destroyed implicitly after its behaviour terminates.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: The termination of a test case, i.e. of the MTC, terminates all PTCs that still exist.
requirements.original: Termination of a test case, i.e. the MTC, terminates all PTCs that still exist, if any.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case SHALL completely create its required configuration of test components and connections when it is invoked.
requirements.original: Since all test components and ports are implicitly destroyed at the termination of each test case, each test case shall completely create its required configuration of components and connections when it is invoked.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: Every test component and every port IS implicitly destroyed at the termination of each test case.
requirements.original: Since all test components and ports are implicitly destroyed at the termination of each test case, each test case shall completely create its required configuration of components and connections when it is invoked.

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The `create` operation SHALL return the unique component reference of the newly created test component instance.
requirements.original: The create operation shall return the unique component reference of the newly created instance.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: A component reference returned by the `create` operation CAN be stored in a variable.
requirements.original: The unique reference to the component will typically be stored in a variable (see clause 6.2.10.1) and can be used for connecting instances and for communication purposes such as sending and receiving.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: A component reference CAN be used for connecting test component instances and for communication purposes such as sending and receiving.
requirements.original: The unique reference to the component will typically be stored in a variable (see clause 6.2.10.1) and can be used for connecting instances and for communication purposes such as sending and receiving.

requirements.subject: ent:component-name
requirements.canonical: A name MAY be associated with a newly created test component instance.
requirements.original: Optionally, a name can be associated with the newly created component instance.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.canonical: The test system SHALL automatically associate the name 'MTC' with the MTC at its creation.
requirements.original: The test system shall associate the names 'MTC' to the MTC and 'SYSTEM' to the test system interface automatically at creation.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.canonical: The test system SHALL automatically associate the name 'SYSTEM' with the test system interface at its creation.
requirements.original: The test system shall associate the names 'MTC' to the MTC and 'SYSTEM' to the test system interface automatically at creation.

requirements.subject: ent:component-name
requirements.canonical: An associated component instance name NEED NOT be unique.
requirements.original: Associated component names are not required to be unique.

requirements.subject: ent:component-name
requirements.canonical: A component instance name IS used for logging purposes only.
requirements.original: The component instance name is used for logging purposes (see clause 19.11) only and shall not be used to refer to the component instance (the component reference shall be used for this purpose) and has no effect on matching.

requirements.subject: ent:component-name
requirements.canonical: A component instance name SHALL NOT be used to refer to the component instance.
requirements.original: The component instance name is used for logging purposes (see clause 19.11) only and shall not be used to refer to the component instance (the component reference shall be used for this purpose) and has no effect on matching.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: The component reference SHALL be used to refer to a component instance.
requirements.original: The component instance name is used for logging purposes (see clause 19.11) only and shall not be used to refer to the component instance (the component reference shall be used for this purpose) and has no effect on matching.

requirements.subject: ent:component-name
requirements.canonical: A component instance name IS NOT considered in matching.
requirements.original: The component instance name is used for logging purposes (see clause 19.11) only and shall not be used to refer to the component instance (the component reference shall be used for this purpose) and has no effect on matching.

requirements.subject: ent:host-id
requirements.canonical: A host id MAY be associated with a newly created test component instance.
requirements.original: Also optionally, a host id can be associated with the newly created component instance.

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.condition: a host id is provided and the component cannot be deployed on the specified host
requirements.canonical: If a host id is provided and the component cannot be deployed on the specified host, the `create` operation SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: If a host id is provided, the create operation shall cause a test case error, if the component cannot be deployed on the specified host.

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The `create` operation MAY be used at any point in a behaviour definition.
requirements.original: Components can be created at any point in a behaviour definition providing full flexibility with regard to dynamic configurations (i.e. any component can create any other PTC).

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: Any test component MAY create any other PTC.
requirements.original: Components can be created at any point in a behaviour definition providing full flexibility with regard to dynamic configurations (i.e. any component can create any other PTC).

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: The visibility of a component reference SHALL follow the same scope rules as the visibility of variables.
requirements.original: The visibility of component references shall follow the same scope rules as that of variables and in order to reference components outside their scope of creation the component reference shall be passed as a parameter or as a field in a message.

ambiguity.issue: A component reference is a value; scope rules apply to the variables storing it.

improper_terms.proper: visibility of variables holding component references

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: the component is referenced outside its scope of creation
requirements.canonical: To reference a test component outside the scope of its creation, the component reference SHALL be passed as a parameter or as a field in a message.
requirements.original: The visibility of component references shall follow the same scope rules as that of variables and in order to reference components outside their scope of creation the component reference shall be passed as a parameter or as a field in a message.

requirements.subject: ent:component-name
requirements.canonical: The name given by the first Expression of the `create` operation SHALL be a `charstring` value.
requirements.original: a) The name given by the first Expression shall be a charstring value and when assigned it shall appear as the first argument of the create function.

requirements.subject: ent:component-name
requirements.condition: a name is assigned
requirements.canonical: When a component name is assigned, it SHALL appear as the first argument of the `create` operation.
requirements.original: a) The name given by the first Expression shall be a charstring value and when assigned it shall appear as the first argument of the create function.

ambiguity.issue: The create operation is called 'create function'.

requirements.subject: ent:host-id
requirements.canonical: The host id given by the second Expression of the `create` operation SHALL be a `charstring` value.
requirements.original: b) The host id given by the second Expression shall be a charstring value and, when assigned, it shall appear as the second argument of the create function.

requirements.subject: ent:host-id
requirements.condition: a host id is assigned
requirements.canonical: When a host id is assigned, it SHALL appear as the second argument of the `create` operation.
requirements.original: b) The host id given by the second Expression shall be a charstring value and, when assigned, it shall appear as the second argument of the create function.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax block (Expression ["," Expression]) does not show how the name is skipped when only a host id is given; the example uses a dash (create(-, "Host4")). The reading that the name may be skipped with "-" is chosen. The operation is also called 'create function'.
readings: When a host id is assigned, it SHALL appear as the second argument of the `create` operation, and the first argument MAY be the not-used symbol "-".
When a host id is assigned, it SHALL appear as the second argument of the `create` operation, and a name SHALL then also be given as the first argument.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The start test component operation IS the operation used to associate a test behaviour with a test component, which then executes that behaviour.
requirements.original: The start operation is used to associate a test behaviour to a test component, which is then being executed by that test component.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The start test component operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `start` "(" ( FunctionInstance | AltstepInstance ) ")".
requirements.original: ObjectReference "." start "(" ( FunctionInstance | AltstepInstance ) ")"

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: Once a PTC has been created, a behaviour SHALL be bound to the PTC and its execution SHALL be started.
requirements.original: Once a PTC has been created and connected, behaviour has to be bound to this PTC and the execution of its behaviour has to be started.

ambiguity.issue: 'created and connected' may be read as a precondition that the PTC is connected before start, or only as the typical order of operations. Connection is not required elsewhere in the standard, so the second reading is chosen.
readings: Once a PTC has been created, a behaviour SHALL be bound to it and started; connecting it before is optional.
A PTC SHALL be created and connected before a behaviour is bound to it and started.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Binding a behaviour to a PTC and starting its execution IS done by the start test component operation.
requirements.original: This is done by using the start operation (as PTC creation does not start execution of the component behaviour).

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The creation of a PTC IS NOT the start of the execution of the component behaviour.
requirements.original: This is done by using the start operation (as PTC creation does not start execution of the component behaviour).

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The start test component operation SHALL bind the required behaviour to the test component.
requirements.original: The start operation shall bind the required behaviour to the test component.

requirements.subject: ent:test-behaviour
requirements.canonical: The behaviour started on a test component IS defined by reference to an already defined function or altstep.
requirements.original: This behaviour is defined by reference to an already defined function or altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: An alive-type PTC MAY perform several behaviours in sequential order.
requirements.original: An alive-type PTC may perform several behaviours in sequential order.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Starting a second behaviour on a non-alive PTC IS a test case error.
requirements.original: Starting a second behaviour on a non-alive PTC or starting a behaviour on a PTC that is still running results in a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.condition: the PTC is still running a behaviour
requirements.canonical: Starting a behaviour on a PTC that is still running IS a test case error.
requirements.original: Starting a second behaviour on a non-alive PTC or starting a behaviour on a PTC that is still running results in a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.condition: a previous behaviour has terminated on the alive-type PTC
requirements.canonical: A behaviour started on an alive-type PTC after termination of a previous behaviour IS executed with the variable values, timers, ports and local verdict as they were left after termination of the previous behaviour.
requirements.original: If a behaviour is started on an alive-type PTC after termination of a previous behaviour, it uses variable values, timers, ports, and the local verdict as they were left after termination of the previous behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:test-behaviour
requirements.condition: a timer was started in the previous behaviour
requirements.canonical: If a timer was started in the previous behaviour of an alive-type PTC, the subsequent behaviour SHOULD be enabled to handle a possible timeout event.
requirements.original: In particular, if a timer was started in the previous behaviour, the subsequent behaviour should be enabled to handle a possible timeout event.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether this is advice to the test writer (the subsequent behaviour should contain a timeout handler) or a requirement on the tool (pending timeout events of component timers are preserved and observable by the next behaviour).
readings: The test writer SHOULD write the subsequent behaviour of an alive-type PTC so that it handles a possible timeout of a timer started in the previous behaviour.
The TTCN-3 tool SHALL preserve timeout events of component timers started in a previous behaviour so that the subsequent behaviour can handle them.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: Every active default IS deactivated when the behaviour of an alive-type PTC is stopped.
requirements.original: In contrast to that, all active defaults are deactivated when the behaviour of an alive-type PTC is stopped.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: When a new behaviour is started on an alive-type PTC, a default IS NOT active.
requirements.original: This means no default is activated when a new behaviour is started on an alive-type PTC.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: The lifetime of a variable or timer IS bound to the scope in which it is declared.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The lifetime of variables and timers is bound to the scope in which they are declared.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: When an alive-type component is stopped, only the component scope remains.
requirements.original: When an alive-type component is stopped, only the component scope is left.

ambiguity.issue: 'only the component scope is left' can mean that only the component scope remains, or that only the component scope is exited (left). The context (s016) supports the first reading.
readings: When an alive-type component is stopped, all scopes of the behaviour are exited and only the component scope remains.
When an alive-type component is stopped, only the component scope is exited.

requirements.subject: ent:test-behaviour
requirements.canonical: A behaviour with a corresponding runs on clause started on an alive-type PTC CAN access only the variable values and timers declared in the component type definition of that PTC from previous behaviours.
requirements.original: This means only variable values and timers declared in the component type definition of an alive-type PTC can be accessed by a behaviour with a corresponding runs on-clause that is started on an alive-type PTC.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-inout-parameter
requirements.canonical: In a start test component operation, an actual inout parameter IS passed to the started function by value, i.e. like an in parameter.
requirements.original: Actual inout parameters will be passed to the function by value, i.e. like in-parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-out-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter list of the function includes an out parameter
requirements.canonical: In a start test component operation, an actual out parameter MAY be omitted using the not-used symbol ("-").
requirements.original: If the function's formal parameter list includes any out parameter the actual parameter list may omit actual out parameters using the dash symbol ("-") or be omitted in the same manner as for actual in parameters with default values (see clause 5.4.2), i.e. they can be omitted in the list notation if all following actual parameters are also omitted and their assignment can be omitted altogether in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-out-parameter
requirements.condition: list notation is used
requirements.canonical: In a start test component operation using list notation, an actual out parameter MAY be omitted if all following actual parameters are also omitted.
requirements.original: If the function's formal parameter list includes any out parameter the actual parameter list may omit actual out parameters using the dash symbol ("-") or be omitted in the same manner as for actual in parameters with default values (see clause 5.4.2), i.e. they can be omitted in the list notation if all following actual parameters are also omitted and their assignment can be omitted altogether in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-out-parameter
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used
requirements.canonical: In a start test component operation using assignment notation, the assignment of an actual out parameter MAY be omitted altogether.
requirements.original: If the function's formal parameter list includes any out parameter the actual parameter list may omit actual out parameters using the dash symbol ("-") or be omitted in the same manner as for actual in parameters with default values (see clause 5.4.2), i.e. they can be omitted in the list notation if all following actual parameters are also omitted and their assignment can be omitted altogether in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-out-parameter
requirements.canonical: A variable given as an actual out parameter in a start test component operation IS left unchanged by the started behaviour, even if the behaviour changes the formal parameter during its execution.
requirements.original: If a variable is given as an actual out parameter, it will remain unchanged by the started behaviour, even if the behaviour changes the formal parameter during its execution.

requirements.subject: ent:return-value
requirements.canonical: A return value or out or inout parameter of a function invoked in a start test component operation IS NOT effective when the started test component terminates.
requirements.original: Possible return values of a function invoked in a start test component operation, i.e. templates denoted by return keyword or inout and out parameters, have no effect when the started test component terminates.

ambiguity.issue: Return values are called 'templates denoted by return keyword'; return values may be values or templates.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a start test component operation SHALL be of component type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a start test component operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:runs-on-clause
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep invoked in a start test component operation SHALL have a runs on clause referencing a component type that is compatible with the test component referenced by the ObjectReference.
requirements.original: b) The function or altstep invoked in a start test component operation shall have a runs `on definition` referencing a component type that is compatible with the newly created component (see clause 6.3.2.7).

ambiguity.issue: 'runs on definition' should be 'runs on clause'; 'newly created component' should be the component addressed by the ObjectReference (which may be an alive-type PTC already used before).

improper_terms.proper: test component referenced by the ObjectReference

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: Every formal parameter of a function or altstep invoked in a start test component operation SHALL be of a component data type.
requirements.original: c) All formal parameters of the function or altstep invoked in a start test component operation shall be of a component data type.

requirements.subject: ent:input-queue
requirements.canonical: When a test component starts execution, messages CAN already be waiting in the incoming queues of its in and inout ports, because these ports start listening when the component is created.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: As in and inout ports starts listening when the component is created, at the moment, when it starts execution there may be messages in the incoming queues of such ports already waiting to be processed.

ambiguity.issue: 'in and inout ports' is not a defined term; ports whose port type allows incoming communication is meant.

improper_terms.proper: ports whose port type declares in or inout messages

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The stop test behaviour operation IS the operation used to stop the execution of a test component by itself or by another test component.
requirements.original: The stop test behaviour operation is used to stop the execution of a test component by itself or by another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The stop test behaviour operation has the syntax `stop` | ( ( ObjectReference | `mtc` | `self` ) "." `stop` ) | ( `all component` "." `stop` ).
requirements.original:
stop | 
  ( ( ObjectReference | mtc | self ) "." stop ) |
  ( all component "." stop )

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component CAN stop the execution of its own currently running test behaviour or of the test behaviour running on another test component by using the `stop` operation.
requirements.original: By using the `stop` test component statement a test component can stop the execution of its own currently running test behaviour or the execution of the test behaviour running on another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: the stopped component is another test component
requirements.canonical: When a test component stops the behaviour running on another test component, the component to be stopped SHALL be identified by its component reference.
requirements.original: If a component does not stop its own behaviour, but the behaviour running on another test component in the test system, the component to be stopped has to be identified by using its component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component MAY stop its own behaviour by a simple `stop` execution statement or by addressing itself in the `stop` operation, e.g. with `self.stop`.
requirements.original: A component can stop its own behaviour by using a simple `stop` execution statement (see clause 19.9) or by addressing itself in the `stop` operation, e.g. by using the `self` operation.

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: Each of the `create`, `start`, `running`, `done` and `killed` operations IS applicable to PTCs only.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: While the `create`, `start`, `running`, `done` and `killed` operations can be used for PTC(s) only, the `stop` operation can also be applied to the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `stop` operation CAN also be applied to the MTC.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: While the `create`, `start`, `running`, `done` and `killed` operations can be used for PTC(s) only, the `stop` operation can also be applied to the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Stopping a test component IS the explicit form of terminating the execution of its currently running behaviour.
requirements.original: Stopping a test component is the explicit form of terminating the execution of the currently running behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:test-behaviour
requirements.canonical: A test component behaviour IS also terminated when its execution reaches the end of the test behaviour started on the component or an explicit `return` statement.
requirements.original: A test component behaviour terminates also by completing its execution upon reaching the end of the test behaviour that is started on this component or by an explicit `return` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-stop
requirements.canonical: Termination of a test component behaviour by reaching its end or by an explicit `return` statement IS called implicit stop.
requirements.original: This termination is also called implicit stop.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-stop
requirements.canonical: An implicit stop IS equivalent in its effects to an explicit stop.
requirements.original: The implicit stop has the same effects as an explicit stop, i.e. the global verdict is updated with the local verdict of the stopped test component (see clause 24).

requirements.subject: ent:global-verdict
requirements.canonical: When a test component stops (implicitly or explicitly), the global verdict IS updated with the local verdict of the stopped test component.
requirements.original: The implicit stop has the same effects as an explicit stop, i.e. the global verdict is updated with the local verdict of the stopped test component (see clause 24).

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.condition: the stopped test component is the MTC
requirements.canonical: If the stopped test component is the MTC, the resources of all existing PTCs SHALL be released.
requirements.original: If the stopped test component is the MTC, resources of all existing PTCs shall be released, the PTCs shall be removed from the test system and the test case shall terminate (see clause 26.1).

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.condition: the stopped test component is the MTC
requirements.canonical: If the stopped test component is the MTC, all existing PTCs SHALL be removed from the test system.
requirements.original: If the stopped test component is the MTC, resources of all existing PTCs shall be released, the PTCs shall be removed from the test system and the test case shall terminate (see clause 26.1).

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.condition: the stopped test component is the MTC
requirements.canonical: If the stopped test component is the MTC, the test case SHALL terminate.
requirements.original: If the stopped test component is the MTC, resources of all existing PTCs shall be released, the PTCs shall be removed from the test system and the test case shall terminate (see clause 26.1).

requirements.subject: ent:non-alive-ptc
requirements.canonical: Stopping a non-alive-type test component (implicitly or explicitly) SHALL destroy it.
requirements.original: Stopping a non-alive-type test component (implicitly or explicitly) shall destroy it and all resources associated with the test component shall be released.

requirements.subject: ent:non-alive-ptc
requirements.canonical: When a non-alive-type test component is stopped, all resources associated with it SHALL be released.
requirements.original: Stopping a non-alive-type test component (implicitly or explicitly) shall destroy it and all resources associated with the test component shall be released.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: Stopping an alive-type component SHALL stop only its currently running behaviour.
requirements.original: Stopping an alive-type component shall stop the currently running behaviour only but the component continues to exist and can execute new behaviour (started on it using the start operation).

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: A stopped alive-type component SHALL continue to exist.
requirements.original: Stopping an alive-type component shall stop the currently running behaviour only but the component continues to exist and can execute new behaviour (started on it using the start operation).

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: A stopped alive-type component CAN execute a new behaviour started on it by the start test component operation.
requirements.original: Stopping an alive-type component shall stop the currently running behaviour only but the component continues to exist and can execute new behaviour (started on it using the start operation).

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: When an alive-type component is stopped, every component variable, component timer and port IS unchanged in its value, contents or state.
requirements.original: Stopping an alive-type component means that all variables, timers and ports declared in the component type definition of the alive-type component keep their value, contents or state.

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.canonical: When an alive-type component is stopped, its local verdict IS kept unchanged.
requirements.original: Furthermore, the local verdict of the component keeps its value.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: When an alive-type component is stopped, every active default IS automatically deactivated.
requirements.original: In contrast to that, all active defaults are automatically deactivated when the alive-type component is stopped.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component SHALL be left in a consistent state after its behaviour is stopped.
requirements.original: The component shall be left in a consistent state after stopping its behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.condition: the behaviour of an alive-type component is stopped during assignment to an already bound variable
requirements.canonical: If the behaviour of an alive-type component is stopped while a new value is assigned to an already bound variable, the variable SHALL remain bound after the component is stopped (with the old or the new value).
requirements.original: For example, if the behaviour of an alive-type component is stopped during assigning a new value to an already bound variable, the variable shall remain bound after the component is stopped (with the old or the new value).

requirements.subject: ent:timer
requirements.condition: the component is stopped during re-starting an already running timer
requirements.canonical: If an alive-type component is stopped while re-starting an already running timer, the timer SHALL be left in the running state after termination of the behaviour.
requirements.original: Similarly, if the component is stopped during re-starting an already running timer, the timer shall be left in the running state after termination of the behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all component` keyword SHALL be used with the `stop` operation by the MTC only.
requirements.original: The all keyword can be used by the MTC only in order to stop all running PTCs but the MTC itself.

ambiguity.issue: The keyword is called 'the all keyword'; the actual construct is `all component`.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `all component.stop` operation IS the stopping of every running PTC, excluding the MTC itself.
requirements.original: The all keyword can be used by the MTC only in order to stop all running PTCs but the MTC itself.

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: A PTC CAN stop the test case execution by stopping the MTC.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: A PTC can stop the test case execution by stopping the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a stop test behaviour operation SHALL be of component type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a stop test behaviour operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The kill test component operation IS the operation used to destroy a test component by itself or by another test component.
requirements.original: The kill test component operation is used to destroy a component by itself or by another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: On a non-alive test component, the `kill` operation IS equivalent in its results to the `stop` operation.
requirements.original: Kill and stop on a non-alive component have the same results, while they differ for alive components: stopping an alive components stops the test behaviour only, the test component continues to exist.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: Stopping an alive-type component IS the termination of its test behaviour only, while the test component continues to exist.
requirements.original: Kill and stop on a non-alive component have the same results, while they differ for alive components: stopping an alive components stops the test behaviour only, the test component continues to exist.

ambiguity.issue: 'alive components' is used instead of 'alive-type components'.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Killing a test component IS the destruction of that test component.
requirements.original: Killing a test component destroys the test component.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The kill test component operation has the syntax `kill` | ( ( ObjectReference | `mtc` | `self` ) "." `kill` ) | ( `all component` "." `kill` ).
requirements.original:
kill | 
  ( ( ObjectReference | mtc | self ) "." kill ) |
  ( all component "." kill )

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation applied on a test component IS terminating the execution of the currently running behaviour of that component, if any.
requirements.original: The kill operation applied on a test component stops the execution of the currently running behaviour - if any - of that component and frees all resources associated to it (including all port connections of the killed component) and removes the component from the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation applied on a test component IS freeing all resources associated with that component, including all its port connections.
requirements.original: The kill operation applied on a test component stops the execution of the currently running behaviour - if any - of that component and frees all resources associated to it (including all port connections of the killed component) and removes the component from the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation applied on a test component IS removing the component from the test system.
requirements.original: The kill operation applied on a test component stops the execution of the currently running behaviour - if any - of that component and frees all resources associated to it (including all port connections of the killed component) and removes the component from the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation MAY be applied by a test component on itself by a simple `kill` statement or by `self.kill`.
requirements.original: The kill operation can be applied on the current test component itself by a simple kill statement or by addressing itself using the self operation in conjunction with the kill operation.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation MAY be applied to another test component.
requirements.original: The kill operation can also be applied to another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: the kill operation is applied to another test component
requirements.canonical: When the `kill` operation is applied to another test component, the component to be killed SHALL be addressed using its component reference.
requirements.original: In this case the component to be killed shall be addressed using its component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.condition: the kill operation is applied on the MTC
requirements.canonical: If the `kill` operation is applied on the MTC (e.g. `mtc.kill`), the test case IS terminated.
requirements.original: If the kill operation is applied on the MTC, e.g. mtc.kill, it terminates the test case.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all component` keyword SHALL be used with the `kill` operation by the MTC only.
requirements.original: The all keyword can be used by the MTC only in order to stop and kill all running PTCs but the MTC itself.

ambiguity.issue: The keyword is called 'the all keyword'; the actual construct is `all component`.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `all component.kill` operation IS stopping and killing every PTC, excluding the MTC itself.
requirements.original: The all keyword can be used by the MTC only in order to stop and kill all running PTCs but the MTC itself.

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'all running PTCs', while EXAMPLE 2 says all (alive-type and normal) PTCs, which includes inactive and stopped alive-type PTCs. The example reading is chosen.
readings: The `all component.kill` operation IS stopping and killing every existing PTC (running, inactive or stopped), excluding the MTC.
The `all component.kill` operation IS stopping and killing only the PTCs that are currently running a behaviour, excluding the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a kill test component operation SHALL be of component type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a kill test component operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `alive` operation IS a Boolean operation that checks whether a test component has been created and is ready to execute or is already executing a behaviour.
requirements.original: The alive operation is a Boolean operation that checks whether a test component has been created and is ready to execute or is executing already a behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `alive` operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | `any component` | `all component` | `any from` ComponentArrayRef ) "." `alive` [ "->" `@index` `value` ValueRef ].
requirements.original:
( ObjectReference | 
   any component | 
   all component |
   any from ComponentArrayRef ) "." alive
  [ "->" @index value ValueRef ]

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: Applied on a non-alive PTC, the `alive` operation IS true if the component is inactive or running a behaviour.
requirements.original: Applied on a normal parallel test component, the alive operation returns true if the component is inactive or running a behaviour and false otherwise.

ambiguity.issue: 'normal parallel test component' is used for a non-alive PTC.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: Applied on a non-alive PTC that is neither inactive nor running a behaviour, the `alive` operation IS false.
requirements.original: Applied on a normal parallel test component, the alive operation returns true if the component is inactive or running a behaviour and false otherwise.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: Applied on an alive-type PTC, the `alive` operation IS true if the component is inactive, running or stopped.
requirements.original: Applied on an alive-type parallel component, the operation returns true if the component is inactive, running or stopped.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: Applied on an alive-type PTC that has been killed, the `alive` operation IS false.
requirements.original: It returns false if the component has been killed.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: Applied on the MTC, the `alive` operation IS true.
requirements.original: Applied on the mtc the operation returns true.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `alive` operation CAN be used similarly to the `running` operation.
requirements.original: The alive operation can be used similar to the running operation (see clause 21.3.6).

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `all component.alive` operation IS true if all PTCs (alive-type or non-alive) are alive.
requirements.original: In particular, in combination with the all keyword it returns true if all (alive-type or normal) PTCs are alive.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: The `any component.alive` operation IS true if at least one PTC is alive.
requirements.original: The alive operation used in combination with the any keyword returns true if at least one PTC is alive.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-component-array
requirements.canonical: When the `any from` component array notation is used with the `alive` operation, each component of the referenced array IS checked in turn, iterating from innermost to outermost dimension and from lowest to highest index for each dimension.
requirements.original: When the any from component array notation is used, the components from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for being inactive or running a function from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.

ambiguity.issue: The components are said to be checked for 'being inactive or running a function', which conflicts with 21.3.5-s004 (a stopped alive-type component is also alive) and ignores altstep behaviours. The reading consistent with the alive semantics of single components is chosen.
readings: With `any from`, each component of the array IS checked for being alive as defined for a single component (for alive-type PTCs, inactive, running or stopped), iterating from innermost to outermost dimension and from lowest to highest index.
With `any from`, each component of the array IS checked only for being inactive or running a function, iterating from innermost to outermost dimension and from lowest to highest index.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-operation
requirements.canonical: When the `any from` component array notation is used, the `alive` operation IS true as soon as the first component found inactive or running a behaviour is reached.
requirements.original: The first component to be found being inactive or running a behaviour causes the alive operation to return the true value.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index of the first component found alive MAY be assigned to an integer variable for a single-dimensional component array, or to an integer array or record of integer variable for a multi-dimensional component array.
requirements.original: The index of the first component found alive can optionally be assigned to an integer variable for single-dimensional component arrays or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional component arrays.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of an `alive` operation SHALL be of component type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of an `alive` operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:component-array
requirements.canonical: The ComponentArrayRef of an `alive` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized component array.
requirements.original: b) The ComponentArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized component array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index redirection of an `alive` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is applied on an `any from` component array construct.
requirements.original: c) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from component array construct.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional component array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional component array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the array.
requirements.original: d) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional component arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the same as the dimension of the array.
requirements.original: e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array, the element type of the integer array or record of integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.original: e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection

requirements.original: f) If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the alive operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the alive operation.

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the alive operation', but the @index clause receives the index of the found component, not the Boolean result. The reading that the stored index value is meant is chosen.
readings: A lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the `@index` clause IS assigned the index value determined by the `alive` operation, and later evaluation of it does not invoke the `alive` operation again.
A lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the `@index` clause IS assigned the Boolean result of the `alive` operation, and later evaluation of it does not invoke the `alive` operation again.

requirements.subject: ent:running-operation
requirements.canonical: The `running` operation IS a Boolean operation that checks whether a test component is already executing a behaviour.
requirements.original: The running operation is a Boolean operation that checks whether a test component is already executing a behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:running-operation
requirements.canonical: The `running` operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | `any component` | `all component` | `any from` ComponentArrayRef ) "." `running` [ "->" `@index` `value` ValueRef ].
requirements.original:
( ObjectReference | 
   any component | 
   all component |
   any from ComponentArrayRef ) "." running
  [ "->" @index value ValueRef]

requirements.subject: ent:running-operation
requirements.canonical: The `running` operation CAN be used by behaviour executing on a test component to ascertain whether behaviour running on a different test component has completed.
requirements.original: The running operation allows behaviour executing on a test component to ascertain whether behaviour running on a different component has completed.

requirements.subject: ent:running-operation
requirements.canonical: The `running` operation returns `true` for the MTC and for a PTC that has been started but not yet terminated or stopped.
requirements.original: The running operation returns true for the mtc and PTCs that have been started but not yet terminated or stopped.

requirements.subject: ent:running-operation

requirements.subject: ent:running-operation

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation

requirements.original: The actions taken by the call operation are dependent on whether the execution of the started behaviour is complete or incomplete.

requirements.subject: ent:complete-execution

requirements.original: If the incomplete execution occurs because the called component was stopped or killed and a catch stop clause is added to the call operation, the StatementBlock of that clause is executed before the call operation terminates.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation

requirements.original: If the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timout clause is added to the call operation, the called component is implicitly stopped and the StatementBlock of the catch timeout clause is executed before the call operation terminates.

ambiguity.issue: Typo 'timout' for 'timeout'.

requirements.canonical: If the execution is incomplete and no matching `catch(stop)` or `catch(timeout)` clause handles it, the `call` operation SHALL end with a test case error.
requirements.original: In all other cases when the execution is incomplete, the call operation ends with a test case error.
